title: Golden Hawaiian-Style Malasadas
summary: Rich, eggy yeasted doughnut balls made with evaporated milk and fried until deep golden.
equipment: large heavy pan or casserole, at least 24 cm wide
wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral oil, for the tray and your hands
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, yeast and salt together in the mixer bowl. Whisk the evaporated milk, warm water, eggs and cooled butter in the jug, pour into the bowl and run the mixer on low for about 2 min until everything comes together.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Turn the speed to medium and knead for about 8 min. The dough should become glossy and elastic but stay sticky and cling to the bowl; do not add extra flour.

steps.title: First rise
steps.text: Scrape the dough into the oiled bowl with an oiled spatula, cover and leave at room temperature for 1.5-2 h until doubled.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Turn the dough onto the oiled tray, press out the air and cut it into 12 pieces of about 60 g. With oiled hands roll each into a smooth ball, flatten it slightly to about 6 cm across and space them well apart.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Cover loosely and leave for 30-45 min. They are ready when they look puffy and a light fingertip press leaves a dent that slowly fills back.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Fill the pan with oil to about 4 cm, keeping it no more than half full, and heat it to 170 °C.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Lower 3-4 balls gently into the oil and fry for 2-3 min a side, holding the oil between 165 and 175 °C, until deep golden with a pale band around the middle. The centre should read about 90 °C on a probe. Drain on the rack.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm on the day they are made.

tips: The most common mistake is frying in oil that is too hot; the outside darkens before the rich centre cooks, so stay at 165-175 °C.
Resist adding flour while kneading; the sticky dough is what makes them so light.
Handle the proved balls gently so they do not deflate.
For the traditional finish, roll them in caster sugar while still warm.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Keep leftovers in an airtight container for up to 1 day and warm in a 160 °C oven for 5 min.
